description.narrative:
Overview <(>&<)> Context
The discovery of major LNG deposits off Mozambique’s northern coast in 2010 came with high expectations of bringing economic prosperity to the country, as the IMF predicted that LNG would transform Mozambique’s economy with revenuesof $500 billion by 2045 and a 24% GDP growth. However, the country’s economic situation has not improved; extreme poverty has remained at61%-63%, and violent insurgency attacks led an IOC to declare a force majeure and increase militarisation of the region and delay investment decisions. Delays are raising questions to the Mozambique society if the LNG projects will result in the country’s economic recovery in view of the US$21.68 Billion debt crisis, which is reinforcing the idea that revenue primarilywould go towards foreigncompanies recovering their investments from the Mozambique government. Global climate change commitments to phase out fossil fuels present additional challenges for Mozambique's gas reserves in the long run.
The viability of theMozambique’s economic recovery is clearly hinged upon the projected fiscal revenues from the LNG projects in Cabo Delgado, yet the risks are too high. The reality, however, is that high militarisation/security costs, the debt crisis and the global climatetransition towards cleaner energy requiringa phase out of fossil fuels will influence the cost of the recovery structure and demand for gas, thus affecting demand and future global gas prices. Our strategy will be two folds; firstly, produce evidenceshowcasing the fiscal risks of continued dependence on LNG to Mozambique's economy and propose alternative economic models for phase out to inform our influencing work; secondly to use evidence to influence existing civil society movement (CSOs working on natural resources, climate justice) to improve their coordination and capacity for evidence influencing to government, parliament, and companies on the risks of LNG; and to influence the Mozambique government and parliament voice on the need to rethinkfurther alternative investment in Mozambique’s LNG sector. The study will assess how the Cabo Delgado LNG project potential fiscal revenue generation is likely to be impacted by the energy transition developments and stalling of the project due to the conflictto ascertain the estimated direct and direct benefits to the economy, and debt implications. It is only through providing detailed scoping into the future that the Mozambican government may start to rethink its development trajectory from possible stranded assets such as the LNG projects given the ballooning debt and poverty crisis.
Outcomes
The project seeks to transform the narrative of LNG for economic prosperity, proposing economic alternative models not hinged on the country’s gas resources.Given the overly high expectations that the Mozambican economy is hinged on LNG projects, it is paramount that society, parliament, and government are provided with a clear picture of the fiscal implications of the risks with the Cabo Delgado LNG projects.Acomprehensive study with empirical evidence will enable better understanding of the LNG projects and possibly transform the narrative on fossil fuel extraction and development towards diversifying the economy in just energy transition pathwayssuch as renewable energy development and critical minerals supply chains. The project will contribute to raising consciousness and a mindset shift amongst the civil society, government, parliament, and general Mozambique public on the current LNG extractivemodel given the impending risks with fossil fuel phaseout and just energy transition global commitments.
Objective 1. By mid-year 2025, undertaken Research to produce one empirical research study on the implications of the global energy transition discourse,debtand conflict in Cabo Delgado on the LNG projects’ potential fiscal revenue generation, and explore economic alternatives to LNG projects.
Milestone 1.1: Project inception meeting launch in the first month for all project partners and relevant stakeholders to understand the project interventions. Milestone 1.2: TORs developed by Oxfam, CDD and CIP in the first month of the project for a structured framework for the research, methodology, timelines, and technical support from strategic partners. Milestone 1.3: One comprehensive research study produced on the fiscal risks of Cabo Delgado LNG and proposals on alternative economic models for phase out within the first half of the project.
Objective 2. By end of 2025 to raise awareness and coalesce thevoices of 1000 civil society organisations and climate justice activists demanding for a Just Energy Transition Development Strategy beyond LNG through learning and advocacyinitiatives, to be produced to advocate for government policies thatenable planning to phase out LNG.
Milestone 2.1: Based on the research study Information, Education and Communication materials for awareness raising and campaign; training packages for trainingand learning events produced between month five and six of theproject. Milestone 2.2: 20 civil society organizations and 200 activists trained for advocacy, campaign and awareness raising on alternative models for Just Energy Transition beyond LNG from month seven to nine of the project. Milestone 2.3: Comprehensiveawareness raising, and research dissemination advocacy strategy developed and implemented with key messages, target audiences, and innovative tactics from month four to six of the project. Milestone 2.4: Local and national campaign and one learning event toraise awareness and build momentum for 100 CSOs and 1000 activists who serve as champions and ambassadors for narrative transformation of gas extraction and development and Just Energy Transition between month six andeleven of the project.
Objective 3. By 2025 To influence the development and implementation of just energy transition policies anchored on rethinking of future alternative investments in the country’s LNG sector and revert the country’s high expectations on LNG Extraction.
Milestone 3.1:Two Policy briefs developed stemming from the research study outlining the risks and limitations of LNG extraction and the opportunities for alternative energy investments, targeting policymakers in the first six months of the project. Milestone 3.2:Roundtables and one on one diplomatic engagements with relevant policy makers, parliamentarians, and civil society organizations, to build support and consensus for Mozambique to develop Just Energy Transition Development Strategy in the last six months of the project.

participating-org.narrative: CDD is a civil society organization established to contribute to the democratic and socio-economic development of Mozambique. Are also a catalyst for the transformational potential of Youth and Guardian of Democracy and Human Rights in Mozambique. CDD'smission isto catalyze capacity development, with a focus on youth; mobilize public opinion and provide an independent space for critical reflection on the challenges to democratization and socio-economic development in Mozambique and the region. The CDDwas founded in 2018 by a group of Mozambican citizens inspired by the Vision of an inclusive, democratic and developmentalist Mozambican society, with respect for Human Rights.
